# S6 replay-guard evidence — set s6replay5 (`certen:s6-replay:v1`, RB10-B12)

This set is a **delta** on `../s6replay1/SPEC.md`, `../s6replay2/SPEC.md`, `../s6replay3/SPEC.md` and `../s6replay4/SPEC.md`.
The wire format and the evidence domain tag are **unchanged**. It adds one refusal, **before** everything the earlier sets
describe: a document longer than **4 MiB (4194304 bytes)** is refused `s6_replay_unproven{evidence_too_large}` without
being read. Every document of at most 4194304 bytes is judged exactly as s6replay1–4 state, so those four sets are
byte-identical and still pass. An implementation is conformant when it judges every vector of s6replay1, s6replay2,
s6replay3, s6replay4 and s6replay5 exactly as stated.

Generated by `GOWORK=off go run ./cmd/s6replayvectors -set s6replay5` (deterministic, no network; `TestS6Replay5Deterministic`).
`MANIFEST` = sha256 of `manifest.json` = `aa2a8ce77f875509e0ab857d7f30158507421111f6ab54da07aa8741c707f07e`. Copy byte for byte.

## 1. Why a bound

The strict reader has **no depth limit** (s6replay4 §3), so a document of any depth is read, and the memory it takes is
bounded only by its input: about 120 bytes per level of an array chain in the Go reader (722 MiB for 6 000 000 levels, a
12 MB file), more for a chain of objects. Honest evidence is far smaller — at most 512 headers of about 1.2 KB of hex, plus
the account and storage proofs, under 1 MiB — so the format states a size bound. `MaxReplayEvidenceBytes = 4194304`
(`pkg/ethproof/replaydecode.go`) is four times the honest maximum, and bounds the deepest document the reader ever sees to
about 2 100 000 levels (about 250 MiB).

## 2. Files

- `NNN_<name>.json` — 10 vectors: `name`, `description`, `settlement` (s6replay1 §1; every vector uses **s6replay1 vector
  001's** settlement), `evidenceFile`, and `expect` (s6replay1 §1: result, state, reason, beforeVerified, established).
- `NNN_<name>.evidence.gz` — the gzip of the exact evidence bytes of vector NNN (gunzip, then use the bytes as they are; no
  newline is added or removed). The large documents are repetitive, so the bytes are stored compressed.
- `manifest.json` — `domain`, `generator`, `spec`, `maxEvidenceBytes` (4194304) and, per vector: `file` and its `sha256`;
  `evidenceFile` and its `evidenceGzSha256`; `evidenceSha256` and `evidenceLength` of the gunzipped bytes; `maxDepth` (the
  deepest nesting of `{` / `[` outside strings); and the `recipe`.
- `MANIFEST` — sha256 of `manifest.json`. `.gitattributes` — `* -text`: the bytes are the contract, never converted.
- No mutation corpus.

The recipe is s6replay4's (§2 there): `evidence = prefix + open × count + core + close × count + suffix` (all strings are
ASCII; × is repetition). An implementation rebuilds the evidence from the recipe and requires it byte-identical to the
gunzipped evidence file and to `evidenceSha256` (Go: `TestS6Replay5Vectors`).

## 3. Decode order — step 0

Go's `DecodeReplayGuardEvidence` (s6replay1 §3, s6replay4 §3) with the new first step:

0. **Size.** `len(evidence) > 4194304` → `s6_replay_unproven{evidence_too_large}` (Go `ReasonEvidenceTooLarge`). The length is
   the only thing looked at: nothing is parsed, so a document over the bound is never `malformed_json`, whatever it is (a
   syntax error, a truncated document, whitespace, 6 000 000 nested arrays). The boundary is exact: **4194304 bytes are
   read normally, 4194305 are refused**.
1. – 4. unchanged (read with no depth limit and the duplicate-key rule, the schema check, the one-of rule, the versions).

An implementation also reads a document of at most 4194304 bytes **with no depth limit and without recursion**: vector 005 is
about 2 097 000 nested arrays (the deepest the bound admits) and must be refused `unknown_field`, not crash. (Go's reader had
recursed over the nesting before this set and died on a 12 MB document of 6 000 000 nested arrays — Go's goroutine stack limit
is a fatal error, not a panic; it now keeps an explicit stack. A TypeScript reader must not recurse over the nesting either.)

The `detail` of the refusal is not part of the verdict a vector pins (`result`, `state`, `reason`, `beforeVerified`,
`established`); Go's reads "the evidence is N bytes, more than the 4194304 bytes the format allows".

**Layer 6.** The evidence is read through the same function when it is the `replayGuard` member of a layer-6 document
(`pkg/execution`, `OutcomeMemberEvidence.UnmarshalJSON`). That path is bounded first by the surrounding document — the
layer-6 document is decoded by `json.Unmarshal` (which refuses more than 10000 nested containers) and is itself a document
the caller holds — and hands the `replayGuard` member to `DecodeReplayGuardEvidence` as raw bytes, so the 4 MiB bound applies
to the member exactly as stated here. The bound does not limit the surrounding document, and this set adds no layer-6 vector.

## 4. The vectors (all with s6replay1 vector 001's settlement)

`pad(n)` = vector 001's evidence behind an unknown first key holding a string of `a`: `{"zzz":"` + `a` × m + `",` + (vector
001's evidence without its `{`), with m chosen so the whole document is n bytes. `closed(n)` = `{"version":"certen:s6-replay:v1","zzz":`
+ `[` × k + `]` × k + `}` + (0 or 1 space), the document n bytes, k as large as n allows.

| files | evidence | length | expect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | s6replay1 vector 001's evidence, byte for byte | 3513 | proven |
| 002 | `pad(4194303)` | 4194303 | refused `unknown_field` |
| 003 | `pad(4194304)` — exactly the bound | 4194304 | refused `unknown_field` |
| 004 | `pad(4194305)` | 4194305 | refused `evidence_too_large` |
| 005 | `closed(4194304)` — about 2.1 million nested arrays | 4194304 | refused `unknown_field` |
| 006 | `closed(4194305)` | 4194305 | refused `evidence_too_large` |
| 007 | the prefix and then `[` opened and never closed | 4194305 | refused `evidence_too_large` (not `malformed_json`) |
| 008 | the prefix, 6 000 000 `[`, 6 000 000 `]`, `}` | 12000040 | refused `evidence_too_large` |
| 009 | 4194304 spaces | 4194304 | refused `malformed_json` (the input ends before a value) |
| 010 | 4194305 spaces | 4194305 | refused `evidence_too_large` |

The pairs 003/004, 005/006 and 009/010 pin the boundary on three shapes: the same document one byte shorter is read and
judged by the earlier rules, one byte longer is refused for its size alone.

Reproduce any evidence: `prefix + open.repeat(count) + core + close.repeat(count) + suffix` from its `recipe`, or gunzip its
`.evidence.gz`; the three must agree with `evidenceSha256` and `evidenceLength`.
